title: Adored French bakery in Seattle undergoes a remodel to make more space for perfect croissants
text:
5 hours ago For Patrick Morin, opening a French bakery in Seattle was a long-held dream that followed him across an ocean.
Before La Parisienne ever opened its doors, Patrick was in Paris, teaching baking classes and sharing his craft with students from around the world. Over time, a pattern emerged. Many of his American students encouraged him to take what he had built in France and bring it to the United States.
Photo by La Parisienne Eventually, he listened.
In 2014, after years of working and building experience in France, Patrick and his wife Christine made the decision to take the leap. On January 20 of that year, they opened La Parisienne in downtown Seattle—a bakery rooted in traditional French techniques, but shaped by a new environment.
It was a fresh start, in more ways than one.
Photo by La Parisienne The name itself reflects that connection back to home. “La Parisienne” is how Parisian women are referred to—a nod to identity, culture, and the everyday elegance that defines life in Paris. It set the tone for what the bakery would become: a place that brings a piece of France into the rhythm of Seattle.
From the beginning, the focus has been clear.
Authenticity. Quality. And a deep commitment to the customer experience.
Every item—whether it’s a crisp baguette, a delicate macaron, or a buttery pain au chocolat—is rooted in traditional methods. There’s no shortcut to that kind of consistency. It comes from discipline, experience, and a respect for the craft.
Photo by La Parisienne But bringing that vision to life in a new country came with its own set of challenges.
Adapting to a different culture, understanding new customer expectations, and navigating language barriers all required patience and flexibility. What worked in Paris didn’t always translate directly to Seattle, and finding that balance took time.
Still, the core idea never changed.
Share the culture. Share the food. And create a place where people feel welcome.
That sense of hospitality is something customers notice right away—often through Christine. Her presence in the bakery adds something intangible but unmistakable. Whether it’s her warmth, her attention to detail, or simply the familiarity of a French accent, she brings a level of authenticity that goes beyond the menu.
Photo by La Parisienne It turns a quick stop into an experience.
Over the years, La Parisienne has become part of the fabric of downtown Seattle. A place where regulars return for their morning coffee and pastry, where newcomers discover something different, and where French tradition quietly blends into the local community.
For Patrick, that connection is what makes the work meaningful.
Sharing something personal—his culture, his craft—and seeing how it resonates with people day after day.
Photo by La Parisienne Looking ahead, the next chapter is already taking shape. Plans are in motion to expand into a larger space, continuing to grow while staying true to the same principles that defined the bakery from the start.
Because for Patrick and Christine, success isn’t just about growth.
It’s about staying rooted in what matters.
And continuing to bring a little bit of Paris to Seattle, one pastry at a time.
La Parisienne
📍 2507 4th Ave, Seattle, WA
📅 Opened: January 20, 2014
👤 Owners: Patrick & Christine Morin
🥐 Specialty: Traditional French pastries, breads, and baked goods
🌐 Website: https://www.laparisienneseattle.com/
Mission: Share authentic French baking traditions while creating a welcoming, customer-focused experience
Vision: Continue growing while preserving the craftsmanship, culture, and hospitality that define La Parisienne
